title: Finding the main idea of a non-fiction text
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Every non-fiction text is mostly about one big point. Finding that point — the main idea — is the first step to understanding what you read. Quick words: non-fiction means writing that tells true facts about real things, not made-up stories.
The main idea is the most important point that the WHOLE text is about.
Read this: 'Bees are very important. They carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps plants make fruit and seeds. Without bees, many of our foods would not grow.'

blocks.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bees are important because they help plants grow our food.
blocks.explain: The whole passage is about why bees matter, so that is the main idea.
blocks.rule: The main idea is the most important point the whole text is about.

practiceItems.prompt: the main idea is the most ___ point of a text
the main idea is what the WHOLE text is ___
a small fact that backs up the main idea is a ___ detail
the main idea is often found in the first or last ___

blocks.content: To find the main idea, ask yourself: 'What is this text mostly about?'

blocks.question: To find the main idea, the best question to ask is:
options: What is the text mostly about?
blocks.explain: The main idea is the overall point, so ask what the text is mostly about.
blocks.rule: Find the main idea by asking what the whole text is mostly about.

practiceItems.prompt: to find the main idea, ask what the text is mostly ___
the main idea covers the ___ text (whole/one line)
the main idea is the big ___ of the text

blocks.question: A passage explains, step by step, how bees make honey. Is the main idea 'bees are yellow' or 'bees make honey through several steps'?
options: 'Bees make honey through several steps' — it covers the whole passage
The passage has no main idea
blocks.explain: The main idea is what the WHOLE passage is mostly about. Since the passage is all about the steps of making honey, that is the main idea. 'Bees are yellow' might be one small detail, not the overall point.
blocks.rule: The main idea is the overall point of the whole passage.
blocks.principle: A main idea covers the whole text, not a single detail.
canonical_solution: The passage is about making honey
'bees are yellow' is a small detail
So the main idea is bees make honey through steps

rubric.look_for: asks what the whole passage is about
chooses the overall point, not a detail
explains main idea covers the whole text

misconceptions.coach: A detail is not the main idea — what is the whole passage about?
Most passages have one overall point.
